_comment: Managed by researchteam. Term-index hooks: merge the `hooks` entries below into .claude/settings.json
(an operator step; researchteam never edits settings.json). Protocol: docs/term-index-protocol.md.
What they do: after Claude writes or edits a file, or runs a shell command, and when a session starts,
they rebuild the term-occurrence index of any project whose documents or register changed. After an
edit to a project document they also report, back to Claude, a discouraged form the edit left in that
file, or what stops a term register that was just edited from loading. The report carries finding codes, term
identifiers, file paths and positions, never document or register text.
What to know before merging: hooks run OUTSIDE the sandbox, on every matching tool call. The command
runs scripts/build_term_index.py, scripts/term_index_engine.py, scripts/check_term_core.py and the pinned core
under scripts/term-index-core/ (checked against its manifest before it runs; the manifest is agent-editable too,
so that check catches drift and accidents, not tampering), files an agent can edit, so merging
this gives those scripts the same trust as the toolchain SessionStart check. The script writes only under Projects/<project>/terminology/,
makes no network call and starts no process. To remove the hooks, delete these entries.
What they do not cover: edits made while no Claude session is running, and other harnesses. Those are
picked up at the next SessionStart, by `term-build`, and by the check inside `validate`.
